destination.name: Phillip Island
destination.tagline: Little penguins, fur seals and surf beaches on an island two hours from Melbourne.
destination.description: Phillip Island lies at the mouth of Western Port, about 140 km from Melbourne, and is joined to the mainland by a 640 m bridge from San Remo to Newhaven. About 40,000 little penguins live here, and the Penguin Parade at Summerland Beach has run since the 1920s. Seal Rocks, off the Nobbies, hosts Australia's largest fur seal colony, up to about 16,000. Australia's first Grand Prix was held on the island in 1928.
whyVisit: Watch penguins come ashore at dusk
See fur seals and wild coastline

goodToKnow.title: Penguin times vary
goodToKnow.detail: Penguins arrive about 5:15pm in June to 8:45pm in January. Viewing areas are outdoors, so bring warm, wind-proof layers.

goodToKnow.title: Bring a car
goodToKnow.detail: The island has little public transport, none to the Penguin Parade. The Nobbies are over five hours' walk from Newhaven.

goodToKnow.title: Avoid night driving
goodToKnow.detail: Skip unpaved roads at night, as kangaroos and wallabies jump out. If you must drive, slow right down.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Summers are mild and fairly dry, so {months} suits penguins, beaches and the coast.

notes: Months based on climate (about 24 C in February vs 13.5 C in July) and busy season; the penguins are there year-round. Wallabies appear in the research's experience list and tips, not in a fact; check photo.
